note.subject: french
note.title: Passé composé activity bank
note.overview: This lesson contains 102 enabled questions. It teaches Passé composé activity bank through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Passé composé activity bank.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Learn each activity as auxiliary + participle + detail.
Most activities use avoir; taught movement/reflexive verbs use être.
With être, check agreement.
Do not reproduce a whole slash-separated row when one activity is requested.
Irregular participles must be recalled exactly.

questionInstructions.label: CONJUGATE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Use the named subject/tense. The bare verb or correct subject + verb is accepted when stated.

questionInstructions.label: CHANGE THE TENSE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Rewrite the entire French phrase in the named tense.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted English and write the complete French answer.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO ENGLISH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted French and write the complete English meaning.

questionInstructions.label: COMPLETE THE FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Do not translate the whole line; write only the word/chunk replacing _____.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « j’ / je » form in the avoir column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives j’ / je → ai for avoir. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « tu » form in the avoir column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives tu → as for avoir. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « il / elle / on » form in the avoir column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives il / elle / on → a for avoir. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « nous » form in the avoir column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives nous → avons for avoir. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « vous » form in the avoir column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives vous → avez for avoir. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « ils / elles » form in the avoir column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives ils / elles → ont for avoir. The subject decides the written ending.

commonMistakes: Copying a whole slash bank instead of the requested activity.
beforeStartingPractice: Read every must-memorise rule.
Cover the answer column and retrieve at least six chunks.
Complete the 60-second self-check.
On each card, read the task label before the French/English stimulus.
note.markingReminder: Accents are displayed and corrected but not deducted. Base spelling, article, subject, verb form, auxiliary, agreement, negative order and required content are still marked.

mustMemoriseRules: Underline the auxiliary, not the participle.

Learn Super Structures as fixed chunks.
Use cover–write–check for spelling targets.

note.subject: french
note.title: Regular present patterns
note.overview: This lesson contains 54 enabled questions. It teaches Regular present patterns through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Regular present patterns.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Regular patterns depend on the subject.
-er: e/es/e/ons/ez/ent.
-ir: is/is/it/issons/issez/issent.
-re: s/s/zero/ons/ez/ent.
Silent endings still matter in writing.
Apply the pattern inside a complete sentence.

questionInstructions.label: CONJUGATE

questionInstructions.label: WRITE ALL FORMS
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Give every named form; reasonable order and separators are accepted.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO ENGLISH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted French and write the complete English meaning.

questionInstructions.label: COMPLETE THE FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Do not translate the whole line; write only the word/chunk replacing _____.

questionInstructions.label: CHOOSE THE ANSWER
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Select exactly one option.

questionInstructions.label: CORRECT THE ERROR
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Find the error and rewrite the whole corrected sentence.

note.subject: french
note.title: Accuracy repair
note.overview: This lesson contains 50 enabled questions. It teaches Accuracy repair through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Accuracy repair.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Use et in 71 and the learned hyphen pattern.
Gymnase is masculine: un grand gymnase.
préférer + action takes an infinitive.
An opinion needs a complete reason.
A real sentence needs its own capital letter and full stop.
Distinguish énervé from énervant.

questionInstructions.label: APPLY THE RULE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Produce the exact item requested by the rule prompt.

questionInstructions.label: ACCURACY REPAIR
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Repair or apply the named accuracy point and use the stated format.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the source example for this target: 70-99 numbers.
workedExamples.why: Use et in 71; use hyphens in compound numbers.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the source example for this target: Gender agreement.
workedExamples.why: gymnase is masculine.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the source example for this target: préférer + infinitive.
workedExamples.why: Conjugate préférer, then keep the second verb infinitive.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the source example for this target: Opinion + reason.
workedExamples.answer: J’aime la musique parce que c’est relaxant.
workedExamples.why: Answer Pourquoi…? with parce que + a full reason.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the source example for this target: Noun vs infinitive.
workedExamples.answer: J’aime le tennis. / J’aime jouer au tennis.
workedExamples.why: Use an article before a noun; no article before the infinitive.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the source example for this target: énervé / énervant.
workedExamples.answer: Je suis énervée. / Le bruit est énervant.
workedExamples.why: énervé = annoyed; énervant = irritating.

commonMistakes: Conjugating the second verb after préférer.

quickCheck.question: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: on lit des poèmes / des romans
quickCheck.answer: on a lu des poèmes / des romans

quickCheck.question: Write the « ils / elles » form in the -er: jouer column.
Write the « je » form in the avoir column.

beforeStartingPractice: Read every must-memorise rule.
Cover the answer column and retrieve at least six chunks.
Complete the 60-second self-check.
On each card, read the task label before the French/English stimulus.
note.markingReminder: Accents are displayed and corrected but not deducted. Base spelling, article, subject, verb form, auxiliary, agreement, negative order and required content are still marked.
